original_question: Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compact space contain a topological copy of the ordinal interval [0, ω2]?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 7.7: "Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum contain a copy of [0, ω2]?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It has the correct class of spaces (scattered semi-Eberlein compacta), the correct forbidden/test subspace ([0, ω2], not [0, ω1]), and the correct topological nature of the question (whether such a compact space can contain a copy of that ordinal interval). It also stays in the right section of the paper rather than drifting into the Banach-space reformulations from Sections 4–6.
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem, specifically Problem 7.7, not as a theorem or conjecture.
To be fully stand-alone, the term "semi-Eberlein" should be defined exactly as in Definition 7.1: a compact space homeomorphic to a compact K ⊆ [-1,1]^Γ such that K ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in K.
If full self-containment is desired, c0(Γ) should be spelled out: c0(Γ) = {x ∈ ℝ^Γ : for every ε > 0, the set {γ ∈ Γ : |x(γ)| > ε} is finite}.
The phrase "topological copy" should be made precise as "a subspace homeomorphic to [0, ω2]".
The ordinal interval [0, ω2] should be specified as carrying its order topology.
If one wants complete topological self-containment, "scattered" can be unpacked as: every nonempty subspace has an isolated point.
refined_question: Can a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum contain a homeomorphic copy of the ordinal interval [0, ω2] with its order topology, where "semi-Eberlein" means homeomorphic to a compact K ⊆ [-1,1]^Γ such that K ∩ c0(Γ) is dense in K?
justification: This draft is targeting the paper’s exact official formulation in Section 7: Problem 7.7 asks precisely whether a scattered semi-Eberlein compactum can contain a copy of [0, ω2]. Definition 7.1 gives the exact meaning of "semi-Eberlein," which is the main hidden hypothesis needed to make the question stand-alone. The nearby discussion also shows why ordinal intervals are part of the section’s agenda: the authors recall that [0, ω1] is not semi-Eberlein and note that the compactum Kϱ behaves roughly like [0, ω1], and then they isolate the [0, ω2] question as the specific open problem they want to emphasize. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 7.7 nearby, so the most faithful refinement is the official question with the topology and the definition of semi-Eberlein made explicit.
